Network.Page.Title: Network
Network.Status.NoAdapter: No usable network adapter — nothing to discover on.
Network.Status.SendingOff: Sending is switched off in Options → Network, so only what this PC already knows can be shown.
Network.Status.ReadyFormat: {0} adapter(s), {1} discovery layer(s). Nothing found yet.
Network.Status.NothingAnswered: Nothing answered. The neighbour table may be empty on a quiet network, and some adapters refuse a multicast join — the log says which.
Network.Options.SendingNote: Everything the Network page sends goes through one guard. Switched off, the page still shows what this PC already knows about its neighbours, but nothing is sent: no discovery traffic and no device actions.
Network.Options.AdaptersNote: An adapter you stop using is left out of discovery, and nothing may be sent through it. An address sweep pings every address on a network, one after another, to find devices that never talk to this PC. Intrusion detection sees that, so allow it only on networks you look after. The permission is for the network the adapter is on now — the same adapter on another network needs its own.
Network.Options.AllowSweep: Allow an address sweep on this network
Network.Options.MaxPackets: Most packets one discovery run may send
Network.Options.MaxSeconds: Longest one discovery run may take, in seconds
Network.Options.LimitsHintFormat: A run may send {0}–{1} packets and take {2}–{3} seconds.
